Independent reconstruction of the link sphere cycles and their rectangular Mayer–Vietoris images
correctness.rationale: For m,b≥2 let a=2m and c=b−1. In deleting z0, the intact join admits the cover Q∪Z in the proof: an allowed face with one B' vertex requires an independent A set (or else a triangle), and a face with at least two B' vertices permits at most one A vertex (or else a square). Q is a simplex with c cones attached along the independence sphere S^(m−1); Z is contractible and J=Q∩Z=K_(a,c). All inclusion maps from the connected graph J to the simply connected Q are nullhomotopic, giving the claimed deletion wedge. For the link the only additional mixed faces beyond Z are the triangles [a0,x,z] with x outside {a0,a1}: omitting the exceptional a0 creates a square; taking x=a1 creates a triangle; taking a third A vertex or a second B' vertex also creates a square. With no B' vertex, the link is the cone-like simplex on {a0,a1} joined with the remaining matching independence complex. Its union with Z has a free circle basis indexed by A minus a0. The triangle for each x and a fixed z1 kills one such circle, and the other triangles attach along null loops. More explicitly, the differences [a0,x,z]−[a0,x,z1] are capped by a disk chain in Z; the relative homology sequence for the triangle attachments shows these give a basis for H2 of the link. The Mayer–Vietoris connecting map in the deletion sends this basis to the corresponding rectangular fundamental cycles in J. These form a subset of a spanning-tree basis, so the composite splits and the link H2 image is primitive in the full deletion H2, including m=2. In the simply connected deletion, Hurewicz classifies each sphere attachment and a unimodular basis change is realized by a self-equivalence of the wedge (identity on any higher sphere summands). The S¹ contributes one new S²; canceling the primitive S² summands leaves c spheres in each indicated degree. The empty-basis case c=1 and coincident-degree case m=2 are both covered.
residual_risks: The eleven recorded field-two tests are corroborative only. Integral torsion-freeness and the all-parameter homotopy equivalence follow from the primitive attaching-map proof.

value.rationale: A single missing edge is the first natural fault of the known intact-join splitting. Internal matching edges already create triangles but give an independence sphere of variable dimension, so this family tests both the low-degree changes seen in pure bipartite fault laws and the fate of a genuinely higher homotopy summand. The primitive rectangular attaching-map argument settles the integral two-degree homotopy response for the whole family and cannot be replaced by the intact type or face enumeration.
residual_risks: The value lies in the precise matching-join one-edge fault family, not in general stability of induced-forest complexes under edge deletion.
